items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: So Dickie, myself, Mack Walker, Harold McFerran, and Don Frye got together again with 'Bull' Williams... and a tenor named Bobby Sands. So Beasley had a 9-piece orchestra to take to Poughkeepsie.

ctx.x: One week before the end of June, Dickie Wells came to my house and said that he had a job for us with a drummer he knew by the name of Dewey Beasley. We met Beasley and he told us that the job was up-state in a place called Poughkeepsie, New York. This was Dewey's home town and the job was at a place called Woodcliff Park, which was an amusement park. The job didn't pay much but we could live and have a little group of our own.

So Dickie, myself, Mack Walker, Harold McFerran, and Don Frye got together again with 'Bull' Williams, an alto player from Dayton, Ohio named Melvin Scott and a tenor named Bobby Sands. So Beasley had a 9-piece orchestra to take to Poughkeepsie. We worked 4 days a week, Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays and played matinees on special occasions and holidays which were not many in the summer.

I had started writing to my estranged wife and we decided to get together again, so she came from Cincinnati after I had been to Poughkeepsie about 3 weeks. The job went fine and Dewey was very happy because he had been able to bring a group to his home town. We got plenty of rest because there was not much activity in Poughkeepsie except for the park which had a dock on the Hudson river and excursion boats stopped there with tourists.
